official_measurement_examples.name: SMP national coverage
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance states 20 Shoreline Management Plans cover the English coast and set a planned approach to flood and coastal erosion risk management through 2105.

official_measurement_examples.name: SMP management approaches
official_measurement_examples.fact: SMPs use four management approaches: hold the line, no active intervention, managed realignment and advance the line; implementation can depend on funding and evidence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Living plan status
official_measurement_examples.fact: SMP Explorer describes SMPs as living plans whose management approaches can change when physical processes, risk, evidence, protected-site constraints or other circumstances change.

official_measurement_examples.name: CCMA definition role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Practice Guidance says Coastal Change Management Areas are used where significant shoreline change is expected over the next 100 years and are informed by SMP evidence and coastal processes.

official_measurement_examples.name: CCMA development test
official_measurement_examples.fact: NPPF allows development in a Coastal Change Management Area only where policy tests including safety over the planned lifetime and no unacceptable impact on coastal change are demonstrated; CCMA status is not a simple automatic-refusal flag.

official_measurement_examples.name: NCERM scenario structure
official_measurement_examples.fact: NCERM provides medium-term to 2055 and long-term to 2105 erosion-risk extents under two management scenarios and three climate scenarios.

official_measurement_examples.name: NCERM uncertainty
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance states NCERM does not show land that will definitely be lost; future erosion may occur anywhere within the risk zone and in extreme cases projections can be exceeded.

official_measurement_examples.name: Marine plan separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Marine plans are statutory plans guiding use and development of English marine areas and must be considered alongside terrestrial planning controls; marine-plan policy assessment is not itself terrestrial planning permission.

core_rules: SMP management approach is strategic policy evidence not a guaranteed funded defence
hold the line does not prove future funding or delivery
no active intervention does not prove an exact erosion date
managed realignment does not define a parcel development boundary by itself
advance the line is not planning permission for private development
SMP versions and amendments must retain effective date and current status
CCMA designation is distinct from NCERM risk geometry
NCERM risk extents are projections not definite future shoreline positions
NCERM scenarios must retain time horizon management scenario and climate scenario
coastal modelling evidence must retain model limitations and uncertainty
marine-plan policy assessment is distinct from terrestrial planning permission
planning permission does not guarantee coastal defence maintenance
coastal policy does not determine ownership access or infrastructure capacity
historic shoreline evidence must not override newer authoritative SMP or NCERM revisions silently
no parcel coastal-change clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
